title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

Rising AppalachiaIn Appalachia, farmers still practice the ancestral tradition of companion planting. Corn grows tall as a trellis, beans climb the corn, and squash provides the ground cover. Rising Appalachia cultivates a similar symbiosis in their music, where Southern folk traditions, New Orleans swamp culture, and Atlanta’s street spirit strengthen each other. Known for their seamless harmonies, songcatching and storytelling, the band has released ten albums and toured throughout North America, South America, Europe, the Celtic Isles, Australia and beyond — performing everywhere from the Telluride Bluegrass Festival and Red Rocks to NPR’s Tiny Desk. All the while, the band has cultivated a devoted grassroots following traveling to communities big and small by train, horseback, bio-diesel bus and sailboat.


Sisters Leah Song and Chloe Smith were raised in Atlanta in a blue collar bohemian family. Their mom was a fiddler, their dad a sculptor. They went to contra dances, wandered the neighborhood forests and had a childhood filled with banjos, harmony singing and other folkways. In her early twenties, while studying art and Indigenous activism in Chiapas, Mexico, Leah returned to her love of folk music. The two sisters then began a wildly creative and successful career that has included busking in New Orleans, traveling with a circus from Southern Italy to Northern Sweden, and collecting songs in Ireland, Bulgaria and Colombia. Rising Appalachia also features the creative musicianship of Duncan Wickel (fiddle, cello), David Brown (upright bass, baritone guitar) and Biko Casini (drums, percussion) — each tradition keepers in their own right.

title: Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan
location: Baker Exhibit Center
description:
Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan
September 26, 2026 – January 10, 2027
Baker Exhibit Hall
“Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan” features Ronan Donovan’s stunning images and videos of wild wolves in the Greater Yellowstone Ecosystem and Ellesmere Island in the high Canadian Arctic. Since 2014, National Geographic Explorer and photographer Ronan Donovan has examined the relationship between wild wolves and humans in order to better understand the animals, our shared history, and what drives the persistent human-wolf conflict. 
The exhibition, created by National Geographic Society and the National Museum of Wildlife Art, will display images and videos—highlighting the contrast between wolves that live in perceived competition with humans and wolves that live without human intervention.“Wolves: Photography by Ronan Donovan” will introduce visitors to the daily lives of wolves in the Arctic—how they hunt, play, travel, and rest in one of the harshest environments on Earth—with unparalleled intimacy. 
About Ronan Donavan
A field biologist turned conservation photographer and filmmaker, Ronan Donovan has explored the human relationship to nature and wildlife on all seven continents. Donovan’s passion for conserving wild animals and wild places was ignited as a child growing up in Vermont and later during his years as a wildlife field biologist researching spotted owls and chimpanzees. He transitioned to visual storytelling as a way to amplify the wildlife researchers and conservationists that Donovan collaborated with. In addition to his National Geographic work on wolves, Donovan has documented human-chimpanzee conflicts in Uganda, and the legacy work of primatologist Dian Fossey focused on mountain gorillas in Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda. Donovan strives to reconnect viewers to the natural world through the lives of our fellow social mammals to highlight our shared past and interwoven future.

title: NC Arboretum Walk: Gardens, Trails, a Stream, & a Plant Sale
description:
Haywood County Walking Meetup Group
We will be joining the Asheville Amblers, AARP, and perhaps some others for this walk. The walk is free, although the Amblers do accept donations (suggested donation: $4.00).

Meet to register inside the Baker Visitor Center at 08:30 a.m. Restrooms are available at the start point. Step-off is at 9:00 a.m.

The walk includes both a guided 5 KM and guided 10 KM option. Both walks have some moderate hills and stair climbing. A significant part of the route is on well-groomed trails with very few obstacles. There are some hills and natural surface paths. Some people will want walking poles.

Walks are through picturesque formal gardens, the Bonsai Exhibition, shaded scenic trails, and paths along a swift flowing stream. The trees should be just starting to color for fall.

After the walk, enjoy the annual plant show and sale.

Dress for the weather; consider a hat and sunscreen. Sneakers should be fine, unless it has rained recently. Be sure to bring plenty of water and a protein snack.

Dogs on leash are welcome but are not allowed in buildings or in the Bonsai Exhibition. Trail strollers should be ok.

The NC Arboretum does not have an admission fee, but they charge $25 per car parking fee (so pack as many people in your car as you can). We recommend for the driver to purchase the lowest level annual membership which includes free parking. (Of course, you may want a higher-level membership, your choice.) We walk at the Arboretum at least six times per year.

title: Southern Blue Ridge Fire Fair
location: Myron Boon Hall, 110
description: Do you have questions about fire in the Southern Blue Ridge Mountains? Join us on September 26th for the 3rd biannual Southern Blue Ridge Fire Fair, a free event for landowners, curious minds and prospective employees of fire and natural resources. We will hear from Adam Warwick, Stewardship Manager for The Nature Conservancy, on the role and importance of fire in our region. This will be followed by a networking event with local natural resource professionals to learn more about job opportunities, funding, technical assistance and other available resources. A free lunch will be provided, followed by a tour of a burn unit on the Warren Wilson College Forest with Dr. Armin Weise, Assistant Professor of Forest Management at Western Carolina University, and Juniper Odell, Prescribed Fire Specialist with the Nature Conservancy. They will be leading a discussion on the ecology of the site and how to properly conduct a controlled burn. The event will be held in 110 Boon Hall and will begin at 9:00am. The event is free.

Whether it’s everyday stress, sadness, or even anger, our suffering can be transformed into inner strength, love, and joy. The first step is understanding its source. In this series, we’ll explore Buddha’s teachings on the Four Noble Truths. The Four Noble Truths are the essence of Buddhist thought and gives us a clear, precise way to understand our life and how to move forward in it. Through teachings and meditation, we’ll discover that suffering comes not from external conditions, but from our own mind. Recognizing this opens the door to transforming our experience and uncovering a more lasting, genuine happiness.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Wellness Day
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
The Asheville Art Museum’s Wellness Day invites visitors to experience the Museum as a place for restoration, reflection, creativity, and community. Throughout the day, guests are encouraged to slow down and engage with art through a series of thoughtfully curated wellness experiences that nurture both mind and body. 
Wellness Day Features:
Afternoon Tea Parlor | Windgate Foundation Atrium | noon–4pm 
Drop-in Yoga on the Plaza | 12:30–1pm 
Drop-in Yoga in the Galleries | 1:30–2pm 
Live Music: Soothing Sounds | Galleries and Windgate Foundation Atrium | noon–4pm 
Drop-in Workshop: Therapeutic Art Making | Studio (level 3) | 1–4pm 
Slow Art Tours | 11:30am–noon, 1–1:30pm, 2:30–3pm 
Mindful Meditation Tours | Self-guided with the Bloomberg App 
William Wegman’s Alphabet Soup | Multipurpose Space (level 1) | noon-4pm 
RESERVE TICKETS NOW 
Museums are uniquely positioned to serve as spaces for wellness. Unlike many public environments, museums invite contemplation, curiosity, and intentional looking. They provide settings where individuals can step away from daily demands and immerse themselves in experiences that inspire wonder, empathy, and personal discovery. Art has the power to help people process emotions, spark meaningful conversations, and connect across diverse perspectives and lived experiences. 
By integrating mindfulness, movement, creative expression, and music into the museum experience, Wellness Day expands the role of the Asheville Art Museum as a community resource dedicated not only to the appreciation of art but also to the holistic well-being of those it serves. The program demonstrates that museums can be active partners in fostering healthier, more connected communities by creating welcoming spaces where creativity becomes a pathway to healing, resilience, and joy. 
  
This program is sponsored by South Arts and the National Endowment for the Arts.

title: Fall Tree ID
description:
Fall Tree ID
With Lauren Lampley 
Friday, September 26  |  1 – 4pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Join this class as we discuss how to use different characteristics and field guides to identify common trees of Western North Carolina found here at the NC Arboretum. We will look at using different characteristics including habitat, bark, buds, growth pattern, leaf shape, and fruit/nut shape to identify trees. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Lauren Lampley began her career at Grandfather Mountain Stewardship Foundation as a Park Naturalist which solidified Lauren’s interests in ecology and a passion for teaching others. She has led walks and hikes in a variety of subjects from Geology to Birding and especially enjoys learning and teaching about our local ecology. She currently works at the NC Arboretum as the Adult Education Coordinator managing all the programming hosted through the Adult Education Department.

Band Members include Dona Cavanagh, fiddle; Zena Rubin, banjo-uke; Maxine Herring, rhythm guitar; Hilary Dirlam, melody guitar; and Celia Millington-Wyckoff, bass.



The five women comprising Nobody’s Darling each have a long history of playing old-time music. Individually they have played in many other bands through the years, including The Carolina Oldtimers, The Pegtwisters, The Zuma House Band, Too Hot To Cook, The Luke Smathers Mountain Swing Band, Honey Holler, and The Carolina Chick Peas.



Stop in to enjoy the music and an afternoon libation or two, perhaps with an early supper or light bite . . . and don't forget your dancing shoes!

description:
Bio:
Homegrown in the rich music scene of Virginia, The Wilson Springs Hotel is a 5-star quintet brought together within a union of genres – a high-energy folk act committed to rock & roll, bluegrass and classic country. 
Their new record “The Day the Bloodroot Bloomed” released on March 20, 2026. The album is an explanation of aging and how you start to lose more people in your life from all kinds of circumstances. How aging is a beautiful thing and leading towards the inevitable at the same time. Overall the record is a description of the beauty and darkness that comes with being alive. 
Forming in 2021, the band released two albums in quick succession, while growing a steadfast audience from their fiery and memorable performances out on the road. The group is named after a historic hotel in Lexington, Virginia, home of lead vocalist/songwriter/guitarist Jacob Ritter. They expertly package dynamic performances full of raw emotion, humor and storytelling, with song-by-song showcases of each player’s talents. You will undoubtedly enjoy the many lovely amenities offered to you during your stay with The Wilson Springs Hotel.

title: Mr. Jimmy
description:
Mr Jimmy is guitarist / vocalist / songwriter,  Jim “Ang” Anderson, who has fronted The Chicago Kingsnakes Blues band for 35 years, to date performing over 4000 shows.



Mr Jimmy writes, sings and plays real-deal Blues, Chicago style.  A lifelong resident of the city's infamous South Side, he has shared the stage with Buddy Guy, Koko Taylor, Little Milton, James Cotton, Junior Wells, Lefty Dizz,  Jimmy Dawkins, Johnny Twist, and the list goes on... In addition to his live performances, he has released 10 albums of original music with the Chicago Kingsnakes and was pleased to announce his debut solo release “All Alone With the Blues” in July 2020. 



Despite a rigorous recording and performance schedule, Mr. Jimmy still found time to produce and host an NPR radio show entitled “Confessin' The Blues” where he interviewed and performed with numerous Blues artists.



 In 2024 Mr Jimmy was voted one of the Best Blues Performers by the readers of Asheville's Mountain Xpress newspaper for the third year in a row



Show 8:30-11:30pm, $10 cover at the door.

Intention: The Attention Economy

What do we pay when we pay attention?

## About Ted Riskin

Ted is interested in anything that can get him out of his head, and music and movement do a pretty good job of that. He hopes to offer music that facilitates an inner journey and invitations that create a shift. While he likes modern electronic music, he can’t create a mix without including lots of natural instruments and voices. Due to a short attention span, he mixes in lots of different musical genres. title: How to Overcome Anger
description:
Meditation in Asheville: Meditation and Modern Buddhism
How to Overcome Anger with Modern Buddhism Teacher Kadam Sharon Lovich

Anger appears in many forms and disguises. Sometimes it manifests as a feeling of stress, other times it may take the form of depression. From the slightest frustration to resentment and embittered rage, anger is an emotion we all need to understand and conquer if we are to enjoy and make the most out of our life. In this series we will explore practical solutions to the problem of anger, deconstructing its actual causes and learning viable alternatives to this painful habit of mind.

title: Shut Up & Write - South Asheville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
Coworking for writers in your area!
Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

Please arrive a few minutes early to say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

A note about the format
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit https://shutupwrite.com

title: Autumn Witch Day Retreat
description:
Awakening Asheville
[Get Your Tickets Here](https://www.eventbrite.com/e/witchy-ways-day-retreat-tickets-1996341264462)

**Calling in all healers, plant parents, mothers, artists, mystics, rebels, and seekers.**
This day is an invitation to remember and return to all that you are.

Together, we’ll spend an autumn afternoon slowing down, dropping in, and reconnecting with ourselves, the season, and one another through ritual, reflection, movement, and a little witchcraft.

As we move through the energies of fall, we’ll explore the seasonal invitation to both release what has run its course and intentionally call in what we’re ready to cultivate next.

**Flow of the Day**
*We’ll begin by gathering in opening circle, setting our intentions, calling in the directions, and grounding into the space through a guided meditation and energetic release.*

*From there, we’ll move into a ceremonial teaching and transmission, exploring the astrological energies of Libra, Scorpio, and Sagittarius alongside sacred feminine archetypes that can support us through the shifting season. Guided journaling, shadow reflection, and group sharing will offer space to bring these teachings into your own lived experience.*

*After a nourishing snack break, we’ll return to the body through intentional yoga and movement, creating space for integration and embodiment.*

*We’ll close our time together with a seasonal ritual. A little autumn witchcraft devoted to releasing what you’re ready to leave behind and calling in what you desire to cultivate. Through apple magic, fire, candlelight, and intention, you’ll create a ritual piece to take home and continue tending throughout the season.*

*Our gathering will conclude with a closing prayer and circle, sealing the magic of the day and honoring what has shifted, opened, or been remembered. Snacks and tea will be served.*

**About your guides**
**Jenn (She/Her)** is an intuitive healer trained Yoga Teacher 9+ years, Reiki Master, Astrologer and Spiritual Coach. She combines her knowledge of the body from 13 years working in physical therapy with all spiritual tools that have contributed to her own healing & spiritual journey to help guide others.
**Vi (They/Them)** is a practicing Witch & Psychic who is a trained Yoga Teacher, Reiki Master, and Tarot Reader. They combine their passions of astrology, divination, dance, and creative expression to help others listen to their intuition.
**Alessandra Mary (she/her)** is a ceremonialist, Akashic priestess, mystic, author, and sacred storyteller devoted to the path of remembrance. Through sacred gatherings and oracular transmissions, she weaves soulful experiences that invite you into deeper connection with synchronicity, authenticity, and the unseen magic woven through everyday life. She stewards the land we will be gathering on.

**PLEASE NOTE: Pre-registration is required for this event to honor the capacity of the space.** If you would like to skip the fees, you can Venmo us $60 [here](https://venmo.com/u/iamalessandramary "https://venmo.com/u/iamalessandramary")

title: Exhibition on Screen | Michelangelo: Love and Death
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Michelangelo – Love and Death offers a cinematic journey through the great chapels and museums of Florence, Rome and the Vatican, to the print and drawing rooms of Europe, to explore Michelangelo’s tempestuous life. The film goes in search of a greater understanding of this charismatic and enigmatic figure, both through his relationships with his contemporaries and his ongoing artistic legacy. The film invites audiences to intimately examine Michelangelo’s art and artistic process – from the Carrara quarries where Michelangelo sourced his marble, to the new technology being used to attribute works. The film also offers a rare chance to get up close to the mesmerizing Rothschild Bronzes, which, following an extensive research project carried out by Academics in Cambridge in 2015, were positively attributed to Michelangelo after over a century of debate.

title: Asheville Foodie Supper Club
description:
AVL Digital Nomads
🍝 Asheville Foodie Supper Club: First Stop, Italia! 🇮🇹

Sunday, September 27 | 6:00 to 9:00 PM
Strada Italiano | 27 Broadway, Downtown Asheville

Limited to 12 people

I’ve been wanting to create something a little different for Asheville Digital Nomads, something smaller, more intimate, and centered around one of my very favorite ways to bring people together. Food. 😁

So, I’m officially launching the Asheville Foodie Supper Club, a monthly culinary adventure where a small group of us will gather around a table, explore Asheville’s ridiculously good food scene, and actually have time to get to know one another.

We’re kicking this thing off with Italian. 🇮🇹🍝🍷

Our first stop is Strada Italiano in downtown Asheville, a cozy Old World-style trattoria serving regional Italian cuisine inspired by both Northern and Southern Italy. Think house-made pasta, risotto, seafood, Italian classics, good wine, and the kind of food that makes you very happy you did not stay home and eat something responsible. 😆

Each month, we’ll choose a different foodie theme. Italian one month, Korean another, Thai, Indian, Mexican, burgers, pizza, seafood, Mediterranean, tapas, and whatever other interesting culinary rabbit holes we decide to wander down.

But the food is only half the idea. The real purpose of the Asheville Foodie Supper Club is to create a different kind of social experience.

Instead of standing around at a larger event having snippets of conversations with 20 different people, we’ll sit around one table with just 8 to 12 of us. We’ll eat. We’ll talk. We’ll laugh. We’ll hear each other’s stories. We’ll linger over dinner and hopefully turn some of those people we recognize from Meetup into people we actually know.

The intention of this event is to meet interesting people, discover really good food and local restaurants, and enjoy conversations that have enough time to go somewhere.

🍷 A Little Supper Club Fine Print

This event is intentionally limited to 12 people, and unlike some of our larger gatherings, this one requires an actual restaurant reservation.

So please only RSVP if you genuinely intend to come. Don’t grab one of the 12 seats as a “maybe.” If something changes, no problem, just update your RSVP as soon as possible so someone on the waitlist has a chance to join us.

Because when there are only 12 chairs at the table, every chair matters.

Strada also offers a nice range of gluten-free, vegetarian, vegan and dairy-free options, so our first Foodie adventure should have something for just about everyone.

Come hungry and ready to connect with some fun and friendly new humans over a yummy meal together.

Welcome to the Asheville Foodie Supper Club. First stop, Italy. 🇮🇹 🍝🍷🍽️

title: Little Butt and Big Butt - 6.3 Mi, 1700 Ft EG
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**Description**
Another higher elevation hike with a fun name and maybe we will see some fall colors. This is on out and back for a total of 6.3 miles and 1700 ft of elevation gain. In the section from Little Butt to Point Misery Gap there are reportedly 365 wooden steps so be prepared for a leg workout. Some sections of the trail may be a bit overgrown so I suggest long pants and it sounds like it will be cold enough that you may want them and a jacket too.

https://www.alltrails.com/explore/trail/us/north-carolina/big-butt-trail

**CARPOOL**
Meet at the Folk Art Center on the BRP at 8am. If you want to go directly to the trailhead, please let me know and use the directions in AllTrails. We will start at the Walker Knob Overlook at about 8:45 am unless we get stuck behind the gravel trucks again.

**WEATHER**
The weather currently looks good for Monday but I'll watch the weather and post a cancellation message by 7:00 AM if there is a chance of severe weather or lightning during this time period..

**QUESTIONS?**
You can message me through MeetUp until 8:00 AM the day of. Cell reception may be sketchy, but you can try to text or call me up to the start of the hike: (508) 965-2333.

description:
AVL Digital Nomads
**The Morning Read: "Can I afford to … ?"**

...Hire? ....Buy the second van? ....Take the bigger space? ....Raise prices? ....Finally pay myself?

It's the most common question owners ask, and it almost never gets answered — because "afford" isn't a feeling and it isn't the bank balance. It's a number, and it isn't on your P&L.

This session is about learning how to find it. If you're a business owner trying to figure out whether you can afford your next move, or a financial professional with a few tricks up your sleeve for helping folks find the answer faster — come. We'll walk through the numbers that help with decisions. Not so you walk out with one answer — so the next time the question comes up, you know how to answer it yourself.

Real numbers from real books, read out loud — like reading tea leaves, except it's math. For owners, buyers, and the people who advise them. No accounting background required.

title: Max Patch Bald; a Saunter
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
Hike a section of the famous Appalachian Trail on top of Max Patch Mountain. This 4,600-foot mountain was cleared and used as pasture in the 1800s. Today, it's a 350-acre tract of open land on a high knob with 360-degree views. On a clear day, you can see from Mt. Mitchell on the east to the Great Smoky Mountains on the south.
Before we get there, we will take a side stop at Little Falls Branch Falls
We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !! This event is dependent on ‘nice’ weather.
**John Muir didn’t like the word ‘hike’. *“We ought to saunter through them reverently, not 'hike' through them.”***
WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.
I currently have 4 driver(s) (=16ppl)
(the group will be split into 2 groups - quicker & slower.)
**WE WILL SPEND (up to) an HOUR AT THE ‘TOP’ TO ‘ENJOY’.** Bring ground cloth, snacks & water.
**MAX PATCH** details::
Difficulty: Well developed easy trail; constant gradual climb.
Length: 2.0 mi total; Total ascent: 275 ft; Pace: **1.5mph**
Before we get there, we will take a side stop at:
**LITTLE FALLS BRANCH FALLS** details:

Head Lamp or Flashlight ***Required in Winter***

**Starting Location:** We will meet at the [Lake Louise Public Bathrooms](https://maps.app.goo.gl/kar8g1usVX7TvjjN8). Call the organizer if you can not find us. 828-290-0886
**If you are running late**: Park at the [Presbyterian Church](https://maps.app.goo.gl/RkA7VmJJy9bFEcF8A) and intercept us.
30 Alabama Ave, Weaverville, NC 28787

**In case of bad weather, the hike will cancel by 4:00 pm, and be rescheduled to the following week.**

**Route:** [Weaverville Wander](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/weaverville-wander-improved-c0c783b)

Cautions: There is a 300 ft stretch along Hamburg Mountain road, which has limited shoulder and will require us to walk single-file.

**Know your pace!** Please note that this is a relatively fast paced hike, 3.2 mph even up hills. On flat sections, we will go faster. Please be aware of your abilities and level of physical fitness. We will stop and wait for people to catch up in certain spots and for water breaks, but we don't want to leave people behind or wait a long time. It will take about 2 - 3 hrs to complete.

**Scenic Asheville Series:** There are [9 hikes in the series](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk/edit?usp=drive_link); hike them all and receive an attractive badge for your backpack. Check your status [HERE](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1XUm-X1_OhxKIi8JU5rhjsW37cAl4yYx8yB_NEjjI5Lk/edit?gid=0#gid=0).
People who hike as guests or plus ones are not tracked on the spreadsheet.
Badgers are always welcome on any hike, even if there's a wait list.

**On-Time Departure**
I typically have 1 or 2 no-shows on my hikes, so we don't wait for people to arrive. If you are late, you'll be left behind.

*Please change your RSVP as soon as you know you can't make it.
- Notes and comments are genuinely appreciated.
*If you have questions, call the hike leader at 828-290-0886.

**Guests**: If you bring a guest/plus one, make sure they know what they are in for. No flip flops. If someone hikes as a guest, the hike will not count toward a badge. If your guest can't keep up, turn back.

**Waitlist**: Please note that people that come to my hikes regularly may be bumped up above newcomers on the waitlist, particularly if they only need 1 or 2 hikes to get their badge. This is to reward people who come regularly, and it is also to be fair to new people who want to be on the hikes. Please keep an eye on your RSVP status.

**Disclaimer and Release of Liability:**

The organizer of this trip is a volunteer and not a professional guide. The function of the organizer is only to organize this trip. Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
***\*\*\*Please note: event listings are moving to the Shut Up & Write! website and this Meetup page will be closed in a few weeks. You will find our Tuesday night events here: [https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2uT2JS7l00)\*\*\****

**Here's how it works.** Show up at or before 6:00. At 6:00, we do some quick introductions. Afterward, for a full 60 minutes (I'll set a timer!) we are heads-down writing. Writing what? A novel? You bet. Some poetry? Sure. Song lyrics? Your resume? That report you need to get to your boss before 8 AM or you'll *need* *to write* that resume? All of the above and more. Just shut up and write.

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

When the timer goes off, we'll check-in with each other and see how it went. Afterward, feel free to stay to chat and get to know your fellow writers, or keep writing, or take off.

Socializing is optional and will happen after (or briefly before) the focused writing. This is a safe space to work on your craft. No one will read or critique your writing.

For more information about our events, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://shutupwrite.com).

**What to Expect**

* Roughly 15 minutes of introductions
* 60 minutes of focused writing (somebody set a timer)!
* Afterward, optional socializing

**Being late is okay:** Just show up and get settled, then check in with the host after the session. (Look for the person with the Shut Up & Write sign).

**What Should I Bring?**

* Whatever you need to be able to write!
* Earbuds/earplugs if you want to block ambient noise.

title: ```Mills River: Bad Fork &; MST – 7 miles, 1275’ ascent
description:
The Asheville Hiking Group
**How to find us**: Mills River Ingles, 3338 Boylston Hwy, in front of gas pumps, closest to Boylston Hwy. Departing on time.
**Directions to Mills River Ingles**: I-26 Exit on NC-280 West, Airport Road---4.3 miles to the Ingles on the right.
Pretty hike along a stream. Up Wash Creek Rd (FS5000) for 0.6 miles. Right on Bad Fork Trail for a 1.8 mile ascent with some steep sections to the BRP at Bent Creek Gap. Left on the Forest Service Rd, under the BRP, right through a tunnel, then right for 1 mile on the MST. Reverse course and return to the BRP for a snack break, then follow the same route back to the cars. Type: In-out. Max elev: 3300’. Avg moving pace: 2.4 mph. Difficulty (1=effortless, 10=hard): 5.5. Dogs: welcome if well-behaved, subject to area restrictions.
**Trailhead**: Wash Creek Campsite.
**Directions to Trailhead**: From Mills River Ingles to the trailhead (6.7 miles): West (left) on North Mills River Rd for 4.8 miles to Wash Creek Rd (FS5000) near the North Mills River Campground. Turn right onto FS5000 for 1.9 miles (mostly gravel) to the first left (FS142). Park at that intersection (limited spaces). Do not turn left across the concrete bridge. Please Note: There is limited parking at the trailhead---please meet at Mills River Ingles for car pool to the trailhead.

\*\*Courtesy (Please read carefully!)\*\* Only sign up if you \\\*truly\\\* plan to come. If you must cancel, please change your status to "Not Going" as soon as possible. Avoid dropping out last-minute so that wait-listers can have sufficient notice. And please please PLEASE don't be a no-show.

title: A Call to Action with The Conservation Alliance
description:
Join us at The Mule for an evening built around community and connection, celebrating the people and organizations working to protect the land, water, and wildlife we all care about. That same week, outdoor industry and media professionals will be gathering in Asheville for the Outdoor Media Summit so we wanted to bring that same energy to all of you, celebrating the people and organizations working to protect the land, water, and wildlife we all care about.Local and regional nonprofits will have tables set up around the taproom, so you can walk around, ask questions, and talk directly with the people doing this work. Come learn how to support parks, forests, and the places you love. 
The evening also coincides with the Outdoor Media Summit, bringing outdoor industry and media professionals to Asheville that same week — a great time to bring our own community together around the same spirit. 
A portion of the evening’s proceeds will support conservation efforts in our region. 
Organizations joining us include The Conservation Alliance, National Parks Conservation Association, The Wilderness Society, Defenders of Wildlife, MountainTrue, GreenWorks, and Outdoor Business Alliance.

title: Shut Up & Write!® in Hendersonville
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Western North Carolina
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:** This event is moving to the Shut Up & Write! website. To RSVP to upcoming session or connect with other local writers, [join the new group page here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2x848mVGaJ ).

If you have any questions, feel free to [reach out here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/contact).

Thanks!
The Shut Up & Write! Team

\-\-\-

Join us for some focused writing time. All writers and all experience levels are welcome and don’t worry, no one will see what you've written. This session is about getting your writing done and meeting other writers in your area.

When you show up, say hello to everyone, grab a drink, and get your writing tools ready. Once you’re all settled, take some time to chat with your fellow writers. Once everyone’s arrived, I will lead quick introductions and then set the timer for our quiet and focused writing session.

Afterward, we’ll have time to chat and get to know each other. We often talk about our successes and challenges as writers. If you don’t have time to stick around, no worries!

**A note about the format**
We don’t host critiques or readings. These events are a safe space for writers of all skill levels and genres to work on their craft, so no one will read or critique your writing.

For our full event schedule, visit [https://shutupwrite.com](https://www.shutupwrite.com).

title: Weekly Critique
description:
AVL Writers
This is the standing weekly critique. Bring anything new you're working on to share with the group. If you don't have a project to share, you are most welcome to attend, discuss, and get inspired.

For our group discussion, please bring at least 8-10 printed copies of your piece. That way, we can all read through each other's work and provide feedback.

Sharing our creative efforts is an important part of the writing process. I'm really looking forward to reading what you've been working on. Don't worry if it's still a rough draft.

If you're having trouble finding us, look for a placard on the table with the group's name.

If you would like to join our group email list for updates regarding contests, events, and more [you can sign up on our website](https://avlwriters.com/).

title: #BreatheWithMe: a wkly online restorative space designed for the Black Community
description:
Awakening Asheville
Contact and Register: SKY Schools https://www.eventbrite.com/e/breathewithme-a-restorative-space-designed-for-the-black-community-tickets-111197697306?aff=ebdssbonlinesearch

Self-Care and Community of Practice Led by Black Facilitators, for the Black Community.

About this Event
"Caring for myself is not self - indulgence; it is self-preservation, and that is an act of political warfare." Audre Lorde

This is an invitation specifically for persons who identify as Black or African American and are overwhelmed with the injustice of the world and are ready to create space in their lives for self-care as we fight for justice for all! (We offer a parallel session for Allies to connect, learn and find support in their work to dismantle racism at allies.eventbrite.com)

We believe Black people deserve a space to relax, reassess, and realign ourselves.

We are a collective of Black stress-management & wellness instructors inspired by human values.

We are here to facilitate your journey of trauma-relief and stress-management.

Imagine how much more energy you will have and how much more powerful you will be when you cut your stress levels in half!

And it can be done in just a few minutes using nothing but your own breath...

Over the last 10 years, we've taught over 100,000 people to do just that.
The key is that your breath is directly linked to your emotions.

This 1-Hour Restorative Session Includes:
-Open, safe space for sharing and self-care for Black people
-Facilitated discussion
-Breath work and meditation

Led by Black facilitators, certified in stress and trauma relief.
Unleash the Hidden Healing Power of the Breath
-SKY Schools

Register for zoom link: https://www.eventbrite.com/e/breathewithme-a-restorative-space-designed-for-the-black-community-tickets-111197697306?aff=ebdssbonlinesearch

title: Cataloochee ELK (GSMNP)
description:
Hendo Fun Friends
**Note: WAITLISTED PEOPLE WILL BE ADDED AS DRIVERS SIGN ON.**
I am going to Cataloochee Valley in the Smoky Mtn Nat'l Pk to explore, picnic and, hopefully, **catch the Elk during their 'rut' bugling.** Up to 16 are welcome to join me.
This event is suitable for non-hikers and “grade school-age” grandchildren.
**Since the storm destroyed much of the valley road, we will park near the church and see how far we can walk into the valley.**
The elk usually overnight in the valley. Usually, by 4-5pm. There is never a guarantee. But, if we get lucky, it's an event not to be missed.
Cataloochee Valley has a historical home, church and barn which we will take time to explore.
**The plan is to arrive early afternoon to give time to explore and 'PICNIC' before the elk 'present' themselves.**
Bring a folding chair, bug spray, camera, water & food.
Hiking NOT required.
**We are the Sloth Hike Team of WNC: “We will get there when we get there.” We dare to go where the ‘real’ hike groups don’t !!**
**[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bsh_8qxUfDY](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bsh_8qxUfDY)**

Google Maps: = “Palmer Chapel Methodist Church”

title: Live Music | Meschiya Lake
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Join us for an evening of lush, intimate sound comprised of stringed instruments, vocal harmonies, and original compositions featuring local musician Meschiya Lake.  
ABOUT THE MUSICIAN  
Meschiya Lake is a dynamic addition to Asheville’s music scene, bringing her powerful vocals, captivating stage presence, and genre-spanning sound to audiences across Western North Carolina. After years of building an acclaimed career in New Orleans, Lake has made Asheville home, blending jazz, blues, Americana, and country influences into performances that are both timeless and fresh. Whether performing intimate originals or beloved classics, Meschiya’s heartfelt storytelling and infectious energy continue to win over local music lovers throughout the region.  
From the stages of Lincoln Center in New York City, to Brazil, Canada, Denmark, The Netherlands, Italy, Russia, the United Kingdom, and Ireland, Meschiya Lake has shown people to express love of life through music and dance.  This passion, seemingly tireless energy, and expert skill have garnered much praise, from NPR’s top ten albums of 2010 to First Lady of Jazz 2013, at the Sun Valley Jazz Festival. But most importantly, back at home in New Orleans, Lake was recognized as Female Performer of the Year, three years running, at the Big Easy Awards, and named Best Female Singer in Offbeat Magazine’s Best of the Beat poll in 2013 and 2014.  
For more information on Meschiya Lake please visit  www.meschiyalake.com

title: Dodgeball Open Play (ages 21+)
description:
Dodgeball AVL
**This is an outdoor event so weather can affect our Meetup. We do not play in rain, temps below 40F, or other adverse weather conditions. Keep on eye on the weather and check group updates to stay informed. ** Waitlisted players, please still consider attending! We only sit players if games have reached capacity. That’s 12v12 for one court and 11v11 for 2 courts. We usually have less people at the beginning after setup (~7:15pm) and the end of the night (after 9pm). That said, we are growing in attendance so play time is not guaranteed for the waitlist and those who do not sign up. Ready to dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge? Come show us what you got with Asheville’s weekly pick-up dodgeball group! We're hosting open play on Thursday night at Asheville Sports Club. We are all about having a great time and getting that adrenaline pumping! Friendly competition is always welcome but fun, safety, and respect for all players are the top priorities. We use squishy rubber dodgeballs that are fun to throw and catch but can sting with enough velocity so no headshots are allowed. Throws should aim at your target’s shoulders or lower. No experience is necessary - we'll teach you the rules. Open to adults 21 and up (bring your ID!). We’re sorry but we cannot accommodate teens or children because there is alcohol on the premises and no one wants to be the person who accidentally hurts a kid. Sign waivers at the bar before playing and enjoy a beverage between games. Rules of the game are covered at the start of the event so please be there at 7pm to learn our format. We loosely follow the USA Dodgeball ruleset with some exceptions to help new players adapt to the game more quickly. Check out our brief rules and expectations summary attached as photos to this Meetup. Here’s an approximate schedule for this event depending on when people arrive: 6:50 - 7:10pm* - Set up courts and mingle - help with set up is appreciated! 7:10 - 7:15pm - Rules and announcements 7:15 - 9:30pm - Play! *If we have enough people once setup is done, we’ll jump into rules and announcements early. We need at least 8 players to start a game, so take advantage of the daylight and try to arrive right at the beginning! Since this is a free event, the more community support we can gather, the better experience everyone will have, especially for the organizers! If you'd like to help, please arrive early or stay late to assist with set up and breakdown. This is a free community offering, however, if you are feeling generous, donations are welcomed to help support and expand our group. We take donations through Pledge here in Meetup or Venmo (dodgeballavl). Cash of course is great too and more effective as there are no platform fees. Your donations genuinely help the group by helping with equipment purchases and raising funds to eventually add another night of dodgeball in an indoor gym. This event would not be possible without the support of Asheville Sports Club. Please consider generously tipping your bartenders and karaoke DJ as well.

title: Evening Group Meditation IN-PERSON or ONLINE
description:

title: Fall Tree ID
description:
Fall Tree ID
With Hannah Lilly and Ben Warfield 
Friday, October 2  |  1pm – 3pm 
BRN – Core  |  BREG – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Join this group as we talk about how to identify the trees of Western North Carolina as they start to lose their leaves. Many of our native species are identifiable even when they’re dormant, and learning this practice is a rewarding and useful skill for all naturalists. We will talk about how to use the bark, twigs, and more to be able to recognize new and familiar trees in our region. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Hannah Lilly is a Botanist and Ecologist interested in the connection between plants, people, and their environment. She studied Biology with a concentration in Ecology, Evolution, and the Environment (BS) at Appalachian State University. She has since worked for the North Carolina and Virginia Natural Heritage Programs conducting field work to monitor rare and sensitive plant species, and to help conserve the truly special natural communities of The Southern Appalachians. Currently, Hannah is a Botany Technician with the US Forest Service- Pisgah in partnership with The Conservation Corps of NC, through which her understanding of WNC ecology and land management is ever growing. Hannah loves to slow down, notice the details, and revel in the whimsy of the natural world with others. 
Ben Warfield graduated from NC State University with a degree in wildlife biology, where he took many classes centered on species identification and ecosystem measurement. While at NC State, he helped teach tree identification and wildlife survey techniques during several field courses offered by the university. He currently works as a botany technician for the United States Forest Service and the Conservation Corps of North Carolina, with most of his work focused on the Pisgah National Forest.

title: Rooted & Regulated: Adaptogens and Herbal Allies for Blood Sugar, Stress & Nervous System Balance
description:
Rooted & Regulated: Adaptogens and Herbal Allies for Blood Sugar, Stress & Nervous System Balance
with Catherine Willows 
Friday, October 2  |  1 – 3:30pm 
Register Here!
  
Plants have long supported the body’s ability to adapt, regulate, and restore balance. In this class, we’ll explore how adaptogens and other plant allies can support stress resilience, nervous system regulation, and healthy blood sugar. Drawing on herbal traditions and a lifestyle medicine lens, we’ll look at how the body’s systems are deeply interconnected, and how the plant world offers gentle, effective, time-tested tools for supporting all of them. Expect an engaging blend of herbal science, traditional use, and practical takeaways — including aligned lifestyle practices — and the chance to meet some of these plants in person. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Catherine Willows is a Registered Nurse, Certified Functional Medicine Health Coach, and Transformational Creativity Coach, and founder of Willows Coaching and Consulting. 
While holding sacred space, she guides adults in awakening their inner creativity — moving beyond the demands of daily life into greater flow, self-discovery, and joy through intuitive art-making processes. 
Catherine believes creativity and our connection to the natural world are deeply interwoven  — both vital pillars of wellbeing, supporting nervous system regulation and inner equanimity, and together essential for living a meaningful, embodied life aligned with purpose and authentic expression.

title: Ginger's Revenge presents: "Sit a Spell" - Traditional Music Sessions with Warren Wilson College
location: Ginger's Revenge
description:
Ginger's Revenge Craft Brewery & Tasting Room and Warren Wilson College are teaming up to launch “Sit a Spell,” a new weekly traditional music jam that will raise funds for the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund while bringing together Asheville’s vibrant roots music community.

 

The open jam sessions will take place Fridays from 6–8 p.m., beginning April 3, at Ginger’s Revenge’s Tasting Room at 829 Riverside Drive, Suite 100. Musicians of all levels are welcome to bring instruments and join the circle, while community members are invited to come listen and enjoy an evening of traditional music. Musical genres will rotate weekly, highlighting a variety of traditions and styles. There will be four Warren Wilson College faculty members who will rotate hosting each week:

 

1st Fridays:  Bluegrass Session with Korey Brodsky2nd Fridays:  Old-Time and Songs with Emolyn Liden3rd Fridays:  Old-Time Session with Clarke Williams4th Fridays:  Celtic Session with Maura ScanlinThrough the partnership, $100 from each weekly session will be donated to the Warren Wilson Music Scholarship Fund, which provides both recognition and financial assistance to outstanding undergraduate students enrolled or planning to enroll in Warren Wilson College who are deserving of funds to meet their necessary college expenses. 

 

“Music has always been a vital part of Warren Wilson’s culture and of the wider Appalachian region,” said Dr. Jason Decristofaro, Professor of Music and Music Department Chair at Warren Wilson College. “This partnership creates a space where the community can gather, share music, and invest directly in opportunities for student musicians.”

 

The scholarship fund helps talented undergraduate musicians meet the costs of college while continuing to develop their craft. Additional donations to the fund will also be welcomed through a QR code available at the events.

 

“Community music jams are about connection and creativity,” said Tammy Clayton, Director of Retail Operations at Ginger’s Revenge. “We’re excited to host these gatherings and help support the next generation of musicians coming out of Warren Wilson.”

 

The inaugural “Sit a Spell” jam will take place Friday, April 3 from 6–8 p.m., with sessions continuing weekly.  For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916

 

 

"Sit a Spell" host bios:


Clarke Williams is a Christian Harmony/Sacred Harp (shape note) singer, and multi-instrumentalist based in Asheville, NC. Clarke is passionate about the shape note singing traditions from across the Southeast, and in particular near his home in Western North Carolina. He helped start the regular bi-weekly Christian Harmony singing in Asheville, and there has brought newer singers into the tradition. Clarke teaches music professionally (fiddle, banjo and guitar), teaching at Warren Wilson College, at the Junior Appalachian Musicians Program (Buncombe, Haywood and Madison Counties), and privately.

 


Emolyn Liden is an artist, educator, musician, and dancer.  She grew up in Brasstown, NC, and loved dancing at the John C. Campbell Folk School.  She has danced with the Cane Creek Cloggers, the Green Grass Cloggers, the Twisty Cuffs (a Cape Breton step-dancing team), and has earned ribbons of every color at old-time music conventions.  She teaches art, music, and dance in public schools, around the country, and currently at Warren Wilson College.  Emolyn also regularly performs old-time fiddle and banjo.  Through her business, The Roving Knitter, Emolyn teaches people to knit and spin, and sells her handmade work.

 


Korey Brodsky is an Asheville-based mandolinist and guitarist. Growing up in Connecticut, he built strong roots in bluegrass music. He has been featured in numerous publications such as Flatpicking Guitar Magazine and Bluegrass Unlimited, was a 2013 IBMA Youth All Star, a member of the 2018 Acoustic Music Seminar, and a graduate of the Berklee College of Music.  Over the years, he has toured and recorded with various local and national bands, including Mile Twelve, the April Verch Band, Nefesh Mountain, and the Tray Wellington Band. In addition to performing, he teaches weekly online and in-person music lessons.

 


Maura Shawn Scanlin is a Boone, NC native who currently makes her home in Asheville, NC.  Maura enjoys performing and collaborating with musicians in a variety of celtic styles:  she performs and tours regularly with duo project Rakish, with guitarist Conor Hearn, and has toured and shared the stage with Seamus Egan, Maeve Gilchrist, Hanneke Cassel, and Karan Casey, among others.  Maura is a two-time U.S. National Scottish Fiddling Champion, and a winner of the Glenfiddich Fiddle Championship in Perthshire, Scotland.  Maura has performed across North America and the United Kingdom, appearing at venues such as Carnegie Hall, Izumi Hall, Jordan Hall, Blair Castle, Shalin-Liu Performance Center, and the Sinclair, among others.  She has performed at festivals including Merlefest, KVMR Celtic Festival, Boston Celtic Music Festival, Bellingham Irish Festival, New Hampshire Highland Games, Grandfather Mountain Highland Games, Rockport Celtic Festival, and Folk Alliance International.  She has been featured on PBS Great Performances’ “Now Hear This” representing the Boston Traditional Music community.  Maura can be found on faculty at various music camps including Sierra Fiddle Camp, Folk College, Boston States Fiddle Camp, Hanneke Cassel’s Pure Dead Fiddle Weekend, Jink & Diddle School of Scottish Fiddling, the Heartbeat Music Project, and Up With Music’s Summer Strings.

title: Oct 2nd Community Cuddles
description:
Asheville Cuddle Collective
Please note- If you want to attend this event you need to purchase a ticket- We advertise in many places and only paid tickets will reserve your space. use the link below to reserve your **[https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/oct-2nd-community-cuddle](https://www.zeffy.com/en-US/ticketing/oct-2nd-community-cuddle)**

**This is a non-sexual touch based event that invites participants to explore platonic intimacy in a safe environment** with like-minded people. We respect personal boundaries and through a supportive framework of mutual agreements that maximize safety and create a space of easy openness and compassionate connection.
At this event we have the chance to normalize touch with clear boundaries; this is a space for respectful, consent-based touch. We allow ourselves to be seen. We have fun.
We welcome people of all backgrounds, genders, ethnicities, relationship styles, sexualities, sizes, and ages (18+).

**THE RULES**

1. Clothes stay on for the whole event.
2. You do not have to touch anyone at this event.
3. You must receive a verbal YES before you touch anyone.
4. Take care of yourself and those you choose to interact with.
5. Speak up if you have a question, concern, or if you need assistance with anything during the event.
6. All emotions are welcome- we love vulnerability.
**WHY CUDDLE?**
Touch is a basic human need, and many of us do not get enough; most people don’t even know they are missing touch, or have a way to ask for touch without sexualizing it. We believe deeply in the power of touch, and the importance of communication and consent in creating a safe space for touch.
CUDDLING WITH STRANGERS
Cuddling with strangers sounds weird or scary to most people. “Will I like it?” “What if someone wants to touch me and I don’t want to?” “What if I say yes and it’s not what I want?” “What if I really want to touch someone and they say no?” These are all normal questions. The answer is that this is a space created to ask for exactly what you want, and receive NOTHING you don’t want. Many people start out nervous at a cuddle event & most are really glad they came.

**Schedule:**
6:50-7pm: Arrive with snacks to share! Get comfortable, meet, mingle, & snack.
7:05pm: Welcome Circle- its mandatory. We will set our container, talk about personal boundaries, communication, & consent.
7:15pm: Icebreakers and connective activities.
8:00pm: Open cuddling! You MUST ask and get a verbal ‘yes’ before touching or cuddling with anybody at this event. If you are not sure how to do this – great! – we will talk about it during the welcome circle.
10:50pm: Closing Circle, cleanup and head home.
**ETIQUETTE**

\*ARRIVE ON TIME: It is important that all participants arrive before the Welcome Circle. The Welcome Circle serves the purpose of creating the safe space for consensual, non-sexual touch between participants and making sure that everyone is informed about consent.

* Please arrive clean & as scent free as possible.
\*BE SOBER: Please do not drink or smoke before or at this event.

**WHAT TO BRING:** personal water bottle and snacks to share, a friend, a date – whatever cuddle accessories you like! The only thing that you are required to bring is a clean and sober you.

These events are not "gender balanced".

**We take individual and group safety seriously!** If you experience, see, or know that one of our participants is not safe to be at this event we want to know about it. We are committed to doing our best to create a safe environment which means that if someone is causing harm (physical or mental) that person is not welcome here (this includes harm that takes place outside of our events). We stand behind survivors and know that some of our participants are here to heal from touch based trauma.

\*refund policy-
Full refund if you cancel 7 days before the event or you cancel due to illness, emergency, or direct exposure to covid/flu.
Credit towards a future event if you cancel more than 3 days before an event.
No refund if you cancel within 2 days of the event or no-show.

Facilitator Kris Hostikka (Kristikka)

Intention: Levity Obscuro

As the leaves fall and the earth draws her breath inward, we too are invited to soften, sink, and return to what is real. We step into the mystery—feeling our way through the dark, trusting the body to know what the mind cannot see. Let us meet the unknown with curiosity, courage, and a little mischief; perhaps the great mystery has a sense of humor too. May we feel the weight of our bodies, the pulse of the blood, the wildness beneath the skin. Tonight, we dance with all of it: the shadow and the spark, the grief and the joy, the animal and the divine. Nothing to hide, nothing to fix—just this wild, beautiful life moving through us, laughing as we find our way home.

Kristikka loves creating a sacred container that takes you on an inward journey utilizing rhythm to move us from quiet embodiment to chaos and down into stillness and integration. title: Sister Sadie & the Kittredge Arts Center Grand Reopening
location: Kittredge Arts Center, Kittredge Theater
description:
On Friday October 2nd at 7 PM, Warren Wilson College celebrates the grand reopening of Kittredge Arts Center, with renowned Bluegrass act Sister Sadie headlining!  The Kittredge Arts Center grand reopening is part of the Warren Wilson College's 2026 Homecoming, and is also a homecoming for Sister Sadie's mandolinist, WWC alum' Rainy Miatke (Music Major, Class of 2025). 

 

Doors open at 6:15 PM with light refreshments, and concert starts at 7 PM.  

 

 

Tickets can be purchased here:  https://wwc-ventures.ticketspice.com/sister-sadie-and-the-kittredge-arts-center-grand-reopening 

 

For more information abuot the event, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro at jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu or (828)545-3916.  

 

 

Sister Sadie Bio:

What started as an accidental band became a force. GRAMMY-nominated. IBMA-decorated. Opry-validated. But for all the
accolades, they were often reduced to one line: an all-female bluegrass band. True—but never the point. Sister Sadie has always
been about the music. The fire. The truth.


Their new album, All Will Be Well, is that truth—loud, fearless, and free. You’ll hear echoes of bluegrass, but what rises is
something bigger: country with claws, Americana with muscle, gospel grit and raw storytelling.


From the haunting “Prodigal Daughter” to the swagger of “Do What You Want” and the aching beauty of “If I Don’t Have You,”
these six women are not performing roles—they’re telling you who they are.


This is Sister Sadie, evolved: bold, bonded, and braver than ever. They're not asking for space. They're taking it.


And they’re just getting started.

 

About Kittredge Arts Center:

Nestled within the beautiful, historic Warren Wilson College campus, the Kittredge Arts Center provides a centralized location for the arts at WWC and WNC. The Center features the 321-seat Kittredge Theater and 80-seat Williams Recital Hall, where music and performance events are featured throughout the year. Kittredge Arts Center is also available as a rental space to organizations looking for an affordable option in a beautiful location for conferences, business retreats, and other events. 

 

For more information, please contact Dr. Jason DeCristofaro (Assistant Professor of Music, Music Department Chair, and Director of Kittredge Arts Center) at 828-545-3916 or jdecristofaro@warren-wilson.edu

description:
Carson Bull is a Nashville-based singer-songwriter making waves in Americana and country music, blending deep Midwestern roots with a voice that cuts through the noise. Originally from Huntertown, Indiana, he draws on the storytelling of Bob Dylan and Waylon Jennings, the grit of Chris Stapleton, and the melodic sensibility of The Eagles to create a sound that lives at the crossroads of heartland rock and modern folk-country—timeless, honest, and distinctly his own.



His debut single “Tomorrow” (May 2025) introduced listeners to a powerful mix of gravel and grace, followed by “Better Off in Blue” (July 2025), which showcased his growing sonic range and lyrical depth. His album “Redshift” shook the Nashville scene with a sold out release show at The 5 Spot in March 2026. Although it has its roots in ancient Asian traditions, the living art of bonsai now enjoys enthusiasts throughout much of the world. This class will provide the basic concepts and skills for novices to begin growing and shaping their own miniature trees. The first half of the class will cover the fundamental horticultural and aesthetic principles of bonsai. It will include such topics as tree selection, watering, pest control, pruning, wiring, and styling. In the second half of the class, each participant will receive a pot, scissors, wire, and planting medium. With guidance from the instructor, the students will create their own bonsai to take home. Materials included in registration. 
Rebecca Ayres is a ceramic artist and gardener. A longtime Arboretum volunteer, she is the assistant to the bonsai curator and helps with overseeing the exhibition garden, the collection and the Carolina Bonsai Expo. She is a member of the Blue Ridge Bonsai Society, where she has taught workshops and classes, and is a graduate of the Arboretum’s Blue Ridge Naturalist program.

description:

**Overview:** This hike is offered as a monthly training hike with the WNC Asheville Chapter of the association of American Pilgrims on the Camino. The route has been announced on the WNC Camino Group [Facebook Group Page](https://www.facebook.com/groups/AVLCamino/announcements).
If you are unfamiliar with the Camino, here are a few links to learn more:

\*[American Pilgrims on the Camino](https://americanpilgrims.org/iwpmap_directory/western-north-carolina/)

* [Stingy Nomads Camino](https://stingynomads.com/camino-de-santiago-walking-guide/)

* [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_(2010_film)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Way_(2010_film))

**Distance:** 5, 7, or 11 miles
**Pace: 3.2 mph**

**Start Times**
**9:30 am**\- Meet at First Congregational Church\, 1735 5th Ave W\, Hendersonville\, NC
**11:15 - 11:45 - Southern Streams coffee across from the FCC church.**

First Section: The first section is a five mile loop. The loop ends at Southern Streams coffee house, which is across from the church where we start. Join us here for coffee, even if you don't have time to walk.

Second Section: Starting at about 11:45 am from Southern Streams coffee, continue through lower Laurel Park. For those who want to exit, you can return to the church on the Ecusta Trail for a total of about 7 miles.

Last Section: To downtown and St. James Church, returning via Ecusta Trail. 10.5 miles total distance.
The church historian will be on hand to give a brief history of the stained glass windows in the church. And we will have cake.

**Caution:** There are a few stretches on busy roads where we will need to walk single file.

Full Route: [Laurel Park Loop](https://www.alltrails.com/explore/map/laurel-park-loop-improved-3937230?u=i&sh=ifwm3x)

Parking: We are meeting at the First Congregational Church. Please carpool if possible.

Dogs: On leash the entire time. The first section is shady, but the pavement may be hot on the last section. Please consider your pup's feet in the heat.

Scenic Asheville Series: This hike counts as a Wildcard substitute on my Scenic Asheville Series. There are 9 [hikes](https://docs.google.com/document/d/11ewlUM9OV8I4npc1cNNsSYOnXI0QPw2isAleXdFzEbI/edit?usp=drivesdk) in the series; hike them all and receive an [attractive badge](https://docs.google.com/drawings/d/1goXUXfzUBqhB4_UeCxodlk4ZPeCCgqZrWK2EUJvk_vI/edit) for your backpack. title: The Art of Presence: Meditation and Reflection in the Museum
location: Asheville Art Museum, 2 South Pack Square, Asheville, NC, 28801, United States
description:
Step into the Museum’s galleries before the doors open for a quiet and contemplative morning of meditation, mindful walking, and reflection. This guided experience invites participants to slow down, settle the nervous system, and explore the Museum as a place of sanctuary, spaciousness, and renewal. 
The session will begin with a brief seated meditation, followed by a walking meditation through selected exhibitions. Along the way, participants will pause with gentle mindfulness prompts designed to support personal reflection, embodied awareness, and a deeper connection with the artwork. Rather than offering art historical interpretation, the experience encourages each participant to notice what arises within them through presence, stillness, and mindful seeing. The group will honor noble silence throughout much of the session with occasional opportunities for brief reflection and sharing. No previous meditation experience is needed. 
Join Joshua on October 3, November 7, and December 5. 
ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST
Joshua Canter is a mindfulness meditation teacher and the founder of True Nature Travels and Education, an Asheville-based organization that has offered transformative retreats and educational experiences around the world for more than 20 years. He holds a master’s degree in Contemplative Psychology and is passionate about making mindfulness accessible, grounded, and relevant to everyday life.

title: Guided Trail Walk
description:
Hit the trails and learn more about The North Carolina Arboretum’s botanically diverse forest with a guided trail walk! April through October, this free hiking program is led by trained volunteer guides who take small groups of participants along woodland trails and through a variety of forest types. Depending on the season and each guide’s area of expertise, topics of discussion may include wildflowers, plant and tree identification, natural history and more. 
Guided trail walks are limited to 15 people, including the guide, and are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age. Groups depart from the Baker Visitor Center Lobby on Tuesdays at 1 p.m. and Saturdays at 10 a.m. and 1 p.m.. 
Walks last 1.5 – 2.5 hours, are approximately one to two miles in length. As this program is held rain or shine, all participants should dress appropriately for the weather. 
There is no pre-registration; walks are first-come first served and sign up sheets are located in the Baker Visitors Center. 
Walks are FREE; however, donations to The North Carolina Arboretum Society are appreciated. Regular parking fees apply. Arboretum Society Members always park free. 
Know Before You Go

Guided Trail Walks are not recommended for guests under 16 years of age.
Guided Trail Walks are rain or shine and all participants should be dressed comfortably and for the weather.
Hikes cover 1-2 miles and last 1.5-2 hours.
Well-behaved leashed pets are welcome to accompany their owners. In the rare case that a pet is disruptive or negatively impacts the experience, the pet and its owner may be asked to excuse themselves from the guided walk.

title: Adult Studio: Beginner Drop Spinning
location: NC
description:
Your life is filled with textiles made from various spun threads and yarn. Come deepen those connections with the fibers that are deeply woven into many aspects of our lives by trying your hand at one of the earliest ways to handspin yarn using a drop spindle. 
Join us for a fun, educational and meditative day of learning the top whirl dropspindle, and maybe some other styles as well. We will prepare, card and spin raw wool fleece to create yarn on a drop spindle. You may have time to try different types of fibers and even different types of spindles. You will get to take home your first handspun yarn, as well as a drop spindle to continue exploring this new skill. 
ABOUT THE TEACHING ARTIST
Jamie Sparks is a multidisciplinary artist and educator with more than 30 years of experience teaching learners of all ages. She has spent more than two decades working with natural fibers, specializing in spinning and felting, and has taught throughout the Southeastern United States, including the John C. Campbell Folk School, Tryon Arts and Crafts School, assisting at Penland School of Crafts and numerous arts councils.  Her fiber arts instruction emphasizes the transformation of raw fleece into finished pieces, combining traditional techniques with an accessible, hands-on approach. Jamie holds an Associates in Metalsmithing from Haywood Community College, where she developed her skills in metalwork and design. Prior to her work in the arts, she focused life as a herbal educator and plant biologist with a focus on the relationship between humans and plants—a passion that continues to influence her creative practice.

title: Naturalist Walk and Talk - Spiders
description:
Naturalist Walk and Talk – Spiders
with Shane Myers 
Saturday, October 3  |  1 – 3pm 
BRN – Elective 
Register Here!
  
Walk around the Arboretum with our staff naturalists and talk about what we see around us. We might see plants and animals, and evidence of them going about their lives in our backyard. Topics will be based on what we see and experience and whatever questions that come up, so every class has the potential to be quite different. 
This month we will focus on the Spiders of the Arboretum. 
This program will take place outside and will follow easy trails and paved walkways. Dress for the weather and prepare to be outside for the entire program time. 
Shane Myers’ interest in nature began as a child with a love of dinosaurs. This quickly grew to include fossils, insects, and reptiles, and learning from the notes his grandparents kept of the birds that came to their feeders in Toledo, Ohio.  He has a Bachelors of Science in Wildlife Biology and did most of his undergraduate work on dragonflies and damselflies. He’s assisted in outreach and education for plant conservation groups, Odonata Groups, and various bird groups. Shane currently works for the Adult Education department at the NC Arboretum.

description:
Forest Bathing Retreat: The Experience of Fall
with Asheville Wellness Tours 
Saturday, October 3  |  2 – 5pm 
Register Here!
  
Join us for a celebration of autumn delights during this restorative afternoon nature connection retreat! From fall foliage to the monarch migration, we will immerse ourselves in the kaleidoscope that is autumn in the Blue Ridge Mountains. Enlivening our senses, calming our weary minds, and lingering in liminality. Together, we will discover natural pathways to equilibrium that will help us navigate life’s ups and downs, as well as the upcoming holiday season. 
Your guide, Kelly Bruce, will lead you on a colorful journey through the fall forest, weaving mindfulness, breathwork, forest bathing and nature therapy together for a restorative afternoon on some of the trails less traveled at the North Carolina Arboretum. We’ll celebrate the experience in community, enjoying a special wild-foraged tea ceremony and snacks. Bring an open mind and an open heart. All are welcome. Presented through Adult & Continuing Education Programs in collaboration with Asheville Wellness Tours. 
Kelly Bruce is a writer, forest therapy guide and nature connection mentor based in Hendersonville, North Carolina. Her mission is to help others deepen their connection with nature, community and Self. Kelly is an Association of Nature and Forest Therapy Certified Guide and Certification Consultant. She is Wilderness First Aid and CPR certified by the American Red Cross.
